name: tee
description: Reads standard input and writes it both to standard output and to one or more files — a T-splitter in the pipe.

flags.description: Append to the files instead of overwriting.
A special useful target: also display on the terminal.

examples.explanation: Appends the line to app.conf AND shows it on screen — handy when sudo blocks a plain >> redirect: echo ... | sudo tee -a /etc/file.
Saves the full build output to a file while still watching it live.
Saves a copy mid-pipeline and continues processing the stream.

about: tee exists to solve a pipe limitation: a normal redirect (>) consumes the stream and ends the pipeline. tee copies it, letting you save and process simultaneously. The sudo tee pattern is essential for writing to root-owned files: command | sudo tee /etc/file > /dev/null.
useCases: Log pipeline output while watching it.
Write to protected files with sudo without losing the pipe.
Branch a stream to multiple files.
mistakes: Forgetting -a and overwriting the target file on every run.
warnings: tee without -a truncates its target file immediately, even if no data arrives.
